plants.name: Basil (Genovese)
plants.growingNotes: Classic Italian basil. Start harvesting when plant reaches 6-8 inches tall. Pinch flowers to encourage leaf growth. Very cold sensitive.
plants.wateringNeeds: Keep soil consistently moist but not waterlogged

plants.name: Basil (Sweet)
plants.sunRequirements: Full sun to partial sun (6-8 hours)
plants.growingNotes: Most common basil variety. Similar to Genovese but slightly sweeter. Start seeds indoors 6-8 weeks before last frost.
plants.wateringNeeds: Regular watering, allow soil to dry slightly between waterings

plants.name: Basil (Thai)
plants.growingNotes: More heat-resistant than sweet basil. Distinctive licorice/anise flavor. Purple stems and flowers. Grows 24-36 inches tall.
plants.wateringNeeds: Regular watering, drought tolerant once established

plants.name: Mint (Spearmint)
plants.growingNotes: Hardy perennial to Zone 5. Can be invasive - consider container growing. Harvest before flowering for best flavor. Can handle temperatures down to -20°F.

plants.name: Summer Savory
plants.growingNotes: Annual herb. Light required for germination - sow on surface. Best harvested just before flowering. Companion plant for beans.
plants.wateringNeeds: Moderate, allow soil to dry between waterings

plants.name: Dill
plants.growingNotes: Protect from strong winds as tall foliage can blow over. Sow seeds 1/4 inch deep. Does not transplant well - direct sow when possible. Self-seeds readily.
plants.wateringNeeds: Regular watering, especially in dry weather

plants.name: Rosemary
plants.growingNotes: Very slow to germinate from seed - start 10-12 weeks before last frost. Perennial in zones 8+. Needs excellent drainage. Can live for decades.
plants.wateringNeeds: Allow soil to dry between waterings, drought tolerant

plants.name: Oregano (Greek)
plants.growingNotes: True Greek oregano has the best flavor for cooking. Perennial in zones 5-10. Harvest just before flowering for best flavor.

plants.name: Thyme (Summer)
plants.growingNotes: Slow to germinate and grow from seed. Start 8-10 weeks before last frost. Harvest just as flowers begin to open. Needs excellent drainage.
plants.wateringNeeds: Water deeply when soil is completely dry

plants.name: Thyme (German Winter)
plants.growingNotes: Extremely cold hardy variety. Start seeds on surface - needs light to germinate. Replace plants after 3-4 years when they become woody.

plants.name: Catnip
plants.growingNotes: Stratify seeds in freezer overnight, then soak 24 hours before sowing. Seeds need light to germinate - barely cover. Harvest when flowering for maximum potency.

plants.name: Cat Grass
plants.scientificName: Avena sativa / Triticum aestivum / Hordeum vulgare
plants.growingNotes: Mix of oat, wheat, and barley grass. Quick growing treat for cats. Harvest when 4-6 inches tall. Can regrow after cutting 1-2 times.

plants.name: Lemon Tree
plants.growingNotes: Plant fresh seeds immediately after removing from fruit. Indoor trees need 8+ hours sunlight or grow lights. Dwarf varieties best for containers. Meyer lemons fruit fastest (4-6 years).
plants.wateringNeeds: Keep soil moist but not waterlogged, good drainage essential

plants.name: Mango Tree
plants.growingNotes: Remove seed from husk before planting. Keep warm and humid for best germination. Indoor trees stay much smaller (6 feet) than outdoor. May never fruit indoors but makes attractive houseplant.
